narrative.overview:
This document records the connected browser implementation in `src/web/`, the public catalogue in `src/components/CatalogView.tsx`, the shared mobile app prompt and the shared website footer. It extends the approved Flixie concept with the existing account and backend. The white/purple wordmark, bundled Manrope, official Pip and F assets, full portrait film artwork and each person's own badge border remain the visual authority.

Compact navigation and tonal lavender or navy surfaces keep personal films and actions easy to scan. Film artwork carries the visual interest; purple marks actions and selected states. Desktop can show personal film, television, friend and plan information in parallel; smaller containers reflow the same content. Public pages distinguish title information, rating sources and deliberately public reviews from personal account content.

This is a scoped browser system. The pre-existing marketing pages and their Inter/Space Grotesk styles remain separate; the approved shared footer brings the same Manrope navigation, support/legal and store destinations to marketing, catalogue, public detail, sign-in and signed-in shells. Corporate pages retain their marketing footer palette; inside the connected browser shell the footer follows the existing app light/dark roles. Browser dimensions here do not replace native Flutter tokens. Product scope and release dependencies live in `PRODUCT.md` and `docs/web-app.md`; surface composition stays in `.impeccable/web-app-brief.md` and `.impeccable/home-footer-brief.md`.
keyCharacteristics: White flix / purple ie in one shared artwork on dark chrome; the latest website instruction aligns visible letter bottoms and uses one font, weight and size.
Bundled Manrope, strong title weights and readable body copy.
Complete portrait artwork, personal badge borders and restrained official Pip/F accents.
Tonal depth, thin separators and rounded controls.

Connected account actions, explicit data states and bounded overlays: all desktop/tablet dialogs are centered; Watch Plan, watch/review, favourite ranking, favourite search and Pick for us also stay centered on phones. The dark photo lightbox fills the phone viewport.

rules.name: The Brand Continuity Rule
rules.body: Extend the existing Flixie identity; this connected browser system does not authorize rebranding the marketing site or native app.

rules.name: The Readable Copy Rule
rules.body: Use the responsive rem reading roles without fixing the HTML root, disabling zoom or suppressing text-size adjustment. Preserve natural wrapping, growing controls and scroll access; compact metadata does not authorize shrinking general copy or hiding meaningful text with ellipses.

rules.name: The Centered Desktop Dialog Rule
rules.body: Every website dialog is centered on desktop/tablet, never bottom-anchored, per the explicit 14 November 2026 preference. The shared choice dialog is fixed with `inset: 0`, `margin: auto` and `calc(100dvh - 48px)` maximum height from (641px) viewport width. Through (640px), generic choices/account actions may use the existing bottom sheet with (12px) edge clearance and `min(85dvh, 850px)` maximum height. Its own contents scroll, with native modal focus behavior; there is no frame-height toggle. Watch/review, favourite ranking, Watch Plan, favourite search and Pick for us retain centered presentations on every device. This website rule does not change native Flutter bottom sheets. The separate mobile app prompt uses safe-area-aware bottom clearance and a viewport cutoff at (820px).

rules.name: The Tonal Depth Rule
rules.body: Use the existing surface hierarchy and lines for content structure; reserve the recorded shadows for overlays and transient feedback.

rules.name: The Complete Artwork Rule
rules.body: Show the full portrait poster and preserve its proportions in shelves, public detail, diary rows and picker results.

dos: **Do** extend the approved Flixie identity and keep this system scoped to the connected browser surfaces.
**Do** show complete portrait artwork with contain fitting and truthful missing-artwork fallbacks.
**Do** preserve each person's awarded and selected badge preference, including an explicit choice of no border.
**Do** use the responsive rem reading roles, preserve browser text enlargement and reflow meaningful titles, metadata and actions.

**Do** center every desktop/tablet website dialog, with bounded scrolling and protected keyboard focus; allow generic phone choices/account actions to use bottom sheets while retaining all-device centered Watch Plan, watch/review, ranking, favourite-search and Pick for us dialogs.
**Do** let avatar choices reflow from their adaptive 6rem minimum and keep Save/Cancel reachable at enlarged text sizes.
**Do** keep favourite ranking centered on phones and desktop, preserve its draft until Save and keep Save/Cancel outside the scrolling list.
**Do** use the dark photo lightbox for gallery images, centered on wider viewports and full-viewport on phones, with complete artwork and persistent controls.
**Do** use Community rating as the primary score label with optional accurate source information; label public reviews and episode spoilers, and render real loading, empty and retry states.
**Do** retain complete provider logos and names, distinguish streaming from rentals and purchases, and keep personal service matches out of public static output.
**Do** keep both desktop store destinations discoverable and mobile download prompts compact and dismissible.
donts: **Don't** promote browser sidebar widths, catalogue header clearance or unused prototype frame rules into the native app system.
**Don't** replace the pre-existing marketing design system as a side effect of extending the connected app.
**Don't** crop film posters into landscape imagery or stretch their proportions.
**Don't** replace individual border preferences with one universal ring or grant an unawarded frame.
**Don't** expose personal diary notes, friend activity, plans or private reviews on public title or search-discovery pages.
**Don't** invent films, availability, reviews, scores or achieved search rankings to fill absent state.
**Don't** turn app download guidance into a redirect or screen-covering install interstitial.
